title: Adic completeness and classical reductions of qcqs finite-model integral inputs
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_F$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $V$. Give $A$ its induced $\ell$-adic norm topology, put $A_V=p_V^*\underline A$ and $P_{n,V}=(A/\pi^n)_V$, and work in the ordinary unbounded derived module-object category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. If $J\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(V,A)$ for the finite constant scalar-model definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible], then $J$ is derived $\pi$-complete [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]: its canonical strict-tower completion unit $J\to R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(J\otimes^L_{A_V}P_{n,V})$ is an isomorphism. For every $n\ge1$, its derived reduction $J_n=J\otimes^L_{A_V}P_{n,V}$ is bounded and constructible and has an étale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] after the finite discrete coefficient equivalence [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence]. There is no Noetherian, characteristic, dimension or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis on $V$.

source.place: Sections 6.5--6.6: agent finite-constant-scalar-model qcqs criterion, not a claim that the topologically Noetherian stratification statements there already have this scope; compare Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Proposition 7.6 and Theorem 7.7 for the adic criterion.
